questions.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre VACUUM y VACUUM FULL?

sentences.text: La forma estándar de VACUUM elimina las versiones muertas de filas en tablas e índices y marca el espacio disponible para su reutilización futura.

citations.quote: removes dead row versions in tables and indexes and marks the space available for future reuse

sentences.text: Sin embargo, no devuelve el espacio al sistema operativo, excepto en el caso especial en que una o más páginas al final de una tabla quedan completamente libres y se puede obtener fácilmente un bloqueo exclusivo de tabla.

citations.quote: it will not return the space to the operating system, except in the special case where one or more pages at the end of a table become entirely free and an exclusive table lock can be easily obtained

sentences.text: En contraste, VACUUM FULL compacta activamente las tablas escribiendo una versión completamente nueva del archivo de tabla sin espacio muerto.

citations.quote: VACUUM FULL actively compacts tables by writing a complete new version of the table file with no dead space

sentences.text: Esto minimiza el tamaño de la tabla, pero puede llevar mucho tiempo y requiere espacio de disco adicional para la nueva copia de la tabla hasta que finaliza la operación.

citations.quote: This minimizes the size of the table, but can take a long time. It also requires extra disk space for the new copy of the table, until the operation completes.

sentences.text: VACUUM FULL requiere un bloqueo ACCESS EXCLUSIVE sobre la tabla y, por tanto, no puede ejecutarse en paralelo con otro uso de la tabla.

citations.quote: VACUUM FULL requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table it is working on, and therefore cannot be done in parallel with other use of the table

sentences.text: La forma estándar de VACUUM puede ejecutarse en paralelo con operaciones de producción de la base de datos.

citations.quote: the standard form of VACUUM can run in parallel with production database operations

questions.question: Why does PostgreSQL need to vacuum to prevent transaction ID wraparound?

sentences.text: PostgreSQL's MVCC transaction semantics depend on being able to compare transaction ID numbers.

citations.quote: MVCC transaction semantics depend on being able to compare transaction ID

sentences.text: Because transaction IDs have limited size (32 bits), a cluster running more than 4 billion transactions would suffer transaction ID wraparound.

citations.quote: transaction IDs have limited size (32 bits)
would suffer transaction ID wraparound

sentences.text: In wraparound, the XID counter wraps around to zero.

citations.quote: the XID counter wraps around to zero

sentences.text: This can make transactions that were in the past appear to be in the future and is described as catastrophic data loss.

citations.quote: transactions that were in the past appear to be in the future
In short, catastrophic data loss

sentences.text: To avoid this, it is necessary to vacuum every table in every database at least once every two billion transactions.

citations.quote: vacuum every table in every database at least once every two billion transactions

sentences.text: Vacuuming solves the problem because VACUUM will mark rows as frozen, indicating that they were inserted by a transaction that committed sufficiently far in the past.

citations.quote: VACUUM will mark rows as frozen

questions.question: ¿Cómo veo el plan de ejecución real de una consulta con tiempos y filas?

sentences.text: Para ver el plan de ejecución que el planificador de PostgreSQL genera para una consulta, se usa EXPLAIN.

citations.quote: This command displays the execution plan that the PostgreSQL planner generates for the supplied statement.

sentences.text: Para obtener el plan real con tiempos y filas, se usa EXPLAIN ANALYZE: la opción ANALYZE hace que la sentencia se ejecute realmente y añade estadísticas reales de tiempo de ejecución, incluido el tiempo total empleado dentro de cada nodo del plan y el número total de filas que devolvió realmente.

citations.quote: The ANALYZE option causes the statement to be actually executed, not only planned.
including the total elapsed time expended within each plan node (in milliseconds) and the total number of rows it actually returned

questions.question: How do I write a recursive query to walk a parent-child hierarchy?

sentences.text: To walk a parent-child hierarchy, use a WITH clause with the RECURSIVE option, which allows a SELECT subquery to reference itself by name.

citations.quote: If RECURSIVE is specified, it allows a SELECT subquery to reference itself by name.

sentences.text: Such a subquery must have the form of a non-recursive term UNION [ ALL | DISTINCT ] recursive term, and the recursive self-reference must appear on the right-hand side of the UNION.

citations.quote: where the recursive self-reference must appear on the right-hand side of the UNION

non_recursive_term
 UNION [ ALL | DISTINCT ]
recursive_term

sentences.text: Only one recursive self-reference is permitted per query.

citations.quote: Only one recursive self-reference is permitted per query.

sentences.text: The documentation shows an example of this typical form: an initial condition, followed by UNION, followed by the recursive part of the query, using a WITH RECURSIVE employee_recursive definition.

citations.quote: Notice the typical form of recursive queries: an initial condition, followed by UNION , followed by the recursive part of the query.
WITH RECURSIVE employee_recursive(distance, employee_name, manager_name) AS (

citations.quote: Be sure that the recursive part of the query will eventually return no tuples, or else the query will loop indefinitely.

sentences.text: Also note that recursive data-modifying statements are not supported, though the results of a recursive SELECT query can be used in a data-modifying statement.

citations.quote: Recursive data-modifying statements are not supported, but you can use the results of a recursive SELECT query in a data-modifying statement.

sentences.text: The optional SEARCH clause computes a search sequence column that can be used for ordering the results of a recursive query in either breadth-first or depth-first order, and the optional CYCLE clause is used to detect cycles in recursive queries.

citations.quote: The optional SEARCH clause computes a search sequence column that can be used for ordering the results of a recursive query in either breadth-first or depth-first order.
The optional CYCLE clause is used to detect cycles in recursive queries.

questions.question: ¿Cómo calculo un total acumulado por cliente con funciones de ventana?

sentences.text: Las funciones de ventana permiten realizar cálculos sobre conjuntos de filas relacionadas con la fila actual de la consulta.

citations.quote: Window functions provide the ability to perform calculations across sets of rows that are related to the current query row

sentences.text: Para agrupar los cálculos por cliente se usa PARTITION BY, que divide las filas de la consulta en particiones procesadas por separado por la función de ventana.

citations.quote: The PARTITION BY clause groups the rows of the query into partitions
The PARTITION BY clause within OVER divides the rows into groups, or partitions

sentences.text: Si se omite PARTITION BY, todas las filas producidas por la consulta se tratan como una sola partición.

citations.quote: Without PARTITION BY , all rows produced by the query are treated as a single partition

sentences.text: Cuando se usa una función de agregado como función de ventana, esta agrega sobre las filas dentro del marco de ventana de la fila actual.

citations.quote: When an aggregate function is used as a window function, it aggregates over the rows within the current row's window frame

sentences.text: Un agregado usado con ORDER BY y la definición de marco de ventana por defecto produce un comportamiento de tipo "running sum", que es lo que da el total acumulado.

citations.quote: An aggregate used with ORDER BY and the default window frame definition produces a “ running sum ” type of behavior

sentences.text: Para obtener la agregación sobre toda la partición (por ejemplo, el total completo del cliente en lugar de un acumulado), se omite ORDER BY o se usa un marco que abarque toda la partición.

citations.quote: To obtain aggregation over the whole partition, omit ORDER BY
ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING

sentences.text: Las llamadas a funciones de ventana solo están permitidas en la lista SELECT y en la cláusula ORDER BY de la consulta.

questions.question: What is the difference between json and jsonb?

sentences.text: PostgreSQL offers two types for storing JSON data: json and jsonb, and they accept almost identical sets of values as input.

citations.quote: PostgreSQL offers two types for storing JSON data: json and jsonb
The json and jsonb data types accept almost identical sets of values as input

sentences.text: The json data type stores an exact copy of the input text, which processing functions must reparse on each execution.

citations.quote: The json data type stores an exact copy of the input text, which processing functions must reparse on each execution

sentences.text: In contrast, jsonb data is stored in a decomposed binary format that is slightly slower to input due to conversion overhead but significantly faster to process because no reparsing is needed, and jsonb also supports indexing.

citations.quote: jsonb data is stored in a decomposed binary format that makes it slightly slower to input due to added conversion overhead, but significantly faster to process, since no reparsing is needed
jsonb also supports indexing, which can be a significant advantage

sentences.text: The json type preserves semantically-insignificant white space between tokens and the order of keys within JSON objects, and all duplicate key/value pairs are kept, though processing functions consider the last value as the operative one.

citations.quote: it will preserve semantically-insignificant white space between tokens, as well as the order of keys within JSON objects
all the key/value pairs are kept
The processing functions consider the last value as the operative one

sentences.text: By contrast, jsonb does not preserve white space, does not preserve the order of object keys, and does not keep duplicate object keys; if duplicate keys are specified in the input, only the last value is kept.

citations.quote: jsonb does not preserve white space, does not preserve the order of object keys, and does not keep duplicate object keys
If duplicate keys are specified in the input, only the last value is kept

sentences.text: In general, most applications should prefer to store JSON data as jsonb, unless there are quite specialized needs, such as legacy assumptions about ordering of object keys.

citations.quote: most applications should prefer to store JSON data as jsonb
unless there are quite specialized needs, such as legacy assumptions about ordering of object keys

questions.question: ¿Cómo convierto un documento JSON en filas y columnas con JSON_TABLE?

sentences.text: JSON_TABLE es una función SQL/JSON que consulta datos JSON y presenta los resultados como una vista relacional que puede accederse como una tabla SQL normal.

citations.quote: JSON_TABLE is an SQL/JSON function which queries JSON data and presents the results as a relational view, which can be accessed as a regular SQL table.

sentences.text: Se puede usar dentro de la cláusula FROM de un SELECT, UPDATE o DELETE y como fuente de datos en una sentencia MERGE.

citations.quote: You can use JSON_TABLE inside the FROM clause of a SELECT , UPDATE , or DELETE and as data source in a MERGE statement.

sentences.text: Toma datos JSON como entrada y emplea una expresión de path JSON para extraer una parte de esos datos y usarla como patrón de filas.

citations.quote: uses a JSON path expression to extract a part of the provided data to use as a row pattern

sentences.text: Cada valor SQL/JSON producido por ese patrón de filas sirve como fuente para una fila separada de la vista construida.

citations.quote: Each SQL/JSON value given by the row pattern serves as source for a separate row in the constructed view.

sentences.text: Para dividir el patrón de filas en columnas, se usa la cláusula COLUMNS, que define el esquema de la vista creada; además, para cada columna se puede especificar una expresión de path JSON separada.

citations.quote: To split the row pattern into columns, JSON_TABLE provides the COLUMNS clause that defines the schema of the created view.
For each column, a separate JSON path expression can be specified to be evaluated against the row pattern

sentences.text: Los datos JSON anidados se pueden extraer con la cláusula NESTED PATH, y las columnas de esos niveles anidados se especifican con una cláusula COLUMNS similar a la de nivel superior.

citations.quote: JSON data stored at a nested level of the row pattern can be extracted using the NESTED PATH clause.
Those columns can be specified using a COLUMNS clause that looks similar to the top-level COLUMNS clause.

sentences.text: Las filas producidas por JSON_TABLE se unen lateralmente a la fila que las generó, por lo que no es necesario unir explícitamente la vista construida con la tabla original que contiene los datos JSON.

citations.quote: The rows produced by JSON_TABLE are laterally joined to the row that generated them, so you do not have to explicitly join the constructed view with the original table holding JSON data.

questions.question: Can MERGE return the rows it inserted or updated?

sentences.text: The returned result is similar to that of a SELECT statement over the row(s) inserted, updated, or deleted by the command.

citations.quote: the result will be similar to that of a SELECT statement

sentences.text: The merge_action() function may be used in the RETURNING list of a MERGE command to identify the action taken for each row.

citations.quote: may be used in the RETURNING list of a MERGE command to identify the action taken for each row

questions.question: ¿Cómo hago un upsert con INSERT ... ON CONFLICT?

sentences.text: Para hacer un upsert se usa la cláusula opcional ON CONFLICT de INSERT, que especifica una acción alternativa a generar un error por violación de unicidad o de restricción de exclusión.

citations.quote: The optional ON CONFLICT clause specifies an alternative action to raising a unique violation or exclusion constraint violation error.

sentences.text: Por cada fila propuesta para inserción, la inserción continúa o, si se viola la restricción o el índice árbitro indicado por conflict_target, se ejecuta la conflict_action alternativa.

citations.quote: For each individual row proposed for insertion, either the insertion proceeds, or, if an arbiter constraint or index specified by conflict_target is violated, the alternative conflict_action is taken.

sentences.text: Con ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING la acción alternativa consiste simplemente en evitar insertar la fila.

citations.quote: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING simply avoids inserting a row as its alternative action.

sentences.text: Con ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE la acción alternativa actualiza la fila existente que entra en conflicto con la fila propuesta para inserción.

citations.quote: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE updates the existing row that conflicts with the row proposed for insertion as its alternative action.

sentences.text: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE garantiza un resultado atómico de INSERT o UPDATE y se conoce como UPSERT.

citations.quote: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarantees an atomic INSERT or UPDATE outcome
This is also known as UPSERT

sentences.text: Para ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE se debe proporcionar un conflict_target.

citations.quote: For ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE , a conflict_target must be provided.

sentences.text: conflict_target especifica los conflictos sobre los que se toma la acción alternativa eligiendo índices árbitro, ya sea mediante inferencia de índice único o nombrando una restricción explícitamente.

citations.quote: Specifies which conflicts ON CONFLICT takes the alternative action on by choosing arbiter indexes
Either performs unique index inference , or names a constraint explicitly.

sentences.text: En la parte DO UPDATE, las cláusulas SET y WHERE pueden acceder a la fila existente con el nombre de la tabla (o alias) y a la fila propuesta con la tabla especial excluded.

citations.quote: The SET and WHERE clauses in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE have access to the existing row using the table's name (or an alias), and to the row proposed for insertion using the special excluded table.

questions.question: How can COPY skip rows with malformed values instead of failing?

citations.quote: The ignore option is applicable only for COPY FROM when the FORMAT is text or csv

questions.question: ¿Cómo cargo un archivo CSV en una tabla con COPY?

sentences.text: Para cargar un archivo CSV en una tabla se usa COPY con la cláusula FROM indicando la ruta del archivo y la opción csv, por ejemplo: COPY postgres_log FROM '/full/path/to/logfile.csv' WITH csv;

citations.quote: COPY postgres_log FROM '/full/path/to/logfile.csv' WITH csv;

sentences.text: Hay que tener en cuenta que COPY confirma todos los datos que importa de una sola vez, de modo que cualquier error provoca que toda la importación falle.

citations.quote: The COPY command commits all of the data it imports at one time, so any error will cause the entire import to fail
any error will cause the entire import to fail

sentences.text: El comando COPY está optimizado para cargar grandes cantidades de filas; es menos flexible que INSERT, pero genera mucha menos sobrecarga en cargas grandes de datos.

citations.quote: The COPY command is optimized for loading large numbers of rows; it is less flexible than INSERT
incurs significantly less overhead for large data loads

sentences.text: Cargar un gran número de filas con COPY es casi siempre más rápido que usar INSERT, incluso si se usa PREPARE y se agrupan varias inserciones en una sola transacción.

citations.quote: loading a large number of rows using COPY is almost always faster than using INSERT

sentences.text: En el formato CSV, los valores de cada registro se separan por el carácter DELIMITER y, en lugar de las reglas de escape del formato de texto estándar de PostgreSQL, se produce y reconoce el mecanismo de escape común de CSV.

citations.quote: The values in each record are separated by the DELIMITER character
it produces and recognizes the common CSV escaping mechanism

questions.question: What is the write-ahead log used for?

sentences.text: Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) is a standard method for ensuring data integrity.

citations.quote: standard method for ensuring data integrity

sentences.text: Under WAL, changes to data files must be written only after WAL records describing those changes have been flushed to permanent storage.

citations.quote: changes to data files (where tables and indexes reside) must be written only after those changes have been logged

sentences.text: After a crash, the database can be recovered using the log, and changes not yet applied to data pages can be redone from WAL records.

citations.quote: any changes that have not been applied to the data pages can be redone from the WAL records

sentences.text: Using WAL reduces disk writes because only the WAL file needs to be flushed to disk to guarantee that a transaction is committed, rather than every data file changed by the transaction.

citations.quote: only the WAL file needs to be flushed to disk to guarantee that a transaction is committed

sentences.text: WAL also makes it possible to support on-line backup and point-in-time recovery.

citations.quote: WAL also makes it possible to support on-line backup and point-in-time recovery

questions.question: ¿Cómo configuro la recuperación a un punto en el tiempo (PITR)?

citations.quote: PITR are configured using normal server configuration parameters

citations.quote: These are set in postgresql.conf or via ALTER SYSTEM

sentences.text: No debe existir un archivo recovery.conf, porque el servidor no arrancará si existe.

citations.quote: The server will not start if a recovery.conf exists.

sentences.text: Debes especificar restore_command para indicar a PostgreSQL cómo recuperar los segmentos WAL archivados.

citations.quote: The one thing that you absolutely must specify is the restore_command

sentences.text: Para recuperar a un punto anterior, se especifica el punto de parada o “recovery target” por fecha/hora, punto de restauración con nombre o ID de transacción.

citations.quote: either by date/time, named restore point or by completion of a specific transaction ID

sentences.text: El punto de parada debe ser posterior al tiempo final de la copia base.

citations.quote: The stop point must be after the ending time of the base backup

sentences.text: Solo se puede usar como máximo uno de recovery_target, recovery_target_lsn, recovery_target_name, recovery_target_time o recovery_target_xid.

citations.quote: At most one of recovery_target , recovery_target_lsn , recovery_target_name , recovery_target_time , or recovery_target_xid can be used

sentences.text: Estos parámetros solo se pueden establecer al iniciar el servidor.

citations.quote: These parameters can only be set at server start.

sentences.text: recovery_target_time especifica la marca de tiempo hasta la cual continuará la recuperación.

citations.quote: This parameter specifies the time stamp up to which recovery will proceed.

questions.question: How do I take an incremental backup with pg_basebackup?

sentences.text: To take an incremental backup with pg_basebackup, specify the --incremental option.

citations.quote: take an incremental backup by specifying the --incremental option

sentences.text: You must supply, as an argument to --incremental, the backup manifest to an earlier backup from the same server.

citations.quote: You must supply, as an argument to --incremental , the backup manifest to an earlier backup from the same server.

sentences.text: In the resulting backup, non-relation files are included in their entirety, but some relation files may be replaced by smaller incremental files containing only changed blocks and metadata needed to reconstruct the current file.

citations.quote: non-relation files will be included in their entirety, but some relation files may be replaced by smaller incremental files

sentences.text: An incremental backup cannot be used directly; pg_combinebackup must first be used to combine it with the previous backups upon which it depends.

citations.quote: An incremental backup cannot be used directly; instead, pg_combinebackup must first be used to combine it with the previous backups upon which it depends.

questions.question: ¿Qué hace pg_combinebackup?

sentences.text: pg_combinebackup se utiliza para reconstruir una copia de seguridad completa sintética a partir de una copia de seguridad incremental y las copias anteriores de las que depende.

citations.quote: pg_combinebackup is used to reconstruct a synthetic full backup from an incremental backup and the earlier backups upon which it depends.

sentences.text: Se deben especificar todas las copias de seguridad necesarias en la línea de comandos, de la más antigua a la más reciente, y la copia reconstruida se escribirá en el directorio de salida indicado mediante la opción -o.

citations.quote: Specify all of the required backups on the command line from oldest to newest.
The reconstructed backup will be written to the output directory specified by the -o option.

sentences.text: Además, pg_combinebackup intentará verificar que las copias de seguridad especificadas formen una cadena de copias válida a partir de la cual se pueda reconstruir una copia completa correcta.

citations.quote: pg_combinebackup will attempt to verify that the backups you specify form a legal backup chain from which a correct full backup can be reconstructed.

questions.question: How do I set up logical replication of a single table to another server?

sentences.text: Logical replication allows replication of data changes on a per-table basis.

citations.quote: Logical replication allows replication of data changes on a per-table basis.

sentences.text: It uses a publish and subscribe model, where subscribers subscribe to publications on a publisher node.

citations.quote: publish and subscribe model with one or more subscribers subscribing to one or more publications on a publisher node

sentences.text: On the publisher, create a publication for the table, as in the example CREATE PUBLICATION pub1 FOR TABLE t1.

citations.quote: CREATE PUBLICATION pub1 FOR TABLE t1

sentences.text: Create the same table on the subscriber, because the schema definitions are not replicated and the published tables must exist on the subscriber.

citations.quote: The schema definitions are not replicated, and the published tables must exist on the subscriber.

sentences.text: Then add a subscription that defines the connection to the other database and the publication to which it subscribes.

citations.quote: A subscription defines the connection to another database and the set of publications (one or more) to which it wants to subscribe.

sentences.text: The subscription is added using CREATE SUBSCRIPTION.

citations.quote: The subscription is added using CREATE SUBSCRIPTION

sentences.text: All subscriptions will copy initial data by default.

citations.quote: All subscriptions will copy initial data by default.

sentences.text: Only regular tables may be the target of replication.

citations.quote: Only regular tables may be the target of replication.

questions.question: ¿Cómo convierto una réplica física en suscriptora lógica con pg_createsubscriber?

sentences.text: Para convertir una réplica física en réplica lógica se usa pg_createsubscriber, que crea una nueva réplica lógica a partir de un servidor standby físico.

citations.quote: pg_createsubscriber creates a new logical replica from a physical standby server.

sentences.text: La herramienta debe ejecutarse en el servidor de destino.

questions.question: ¿Cómo otorgo permiso de solo lectura sobre todas las tablas de un esquema?

sentences.text: Para otorgar el privilegio SELECT a todos sobre todas las tablas (y vistas) que se creen posteriormente en un esquema, la documentación ofrece como ejemplo conceder ese privilegio en el esquema myschema.

citations.quote: Grant SELECT privilege to everyone for all tables (and views) you subsequently create in schema myschema
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA myschema GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO PUBLIC;

sentences.text: Los privilegios de acceso por defecto se establecen precisamente con el comando ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES.

citations.quote: The ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES command is used to set default access privileges.

sentences.text: Los privilegios de acceso se establecen con los comandos GRANT y REVOKE.

citations.quote: The GRANT and REVOKE commands are used to set access privileges.

sentences.text: Ese otorgamiento se puede deshacer para que las tablas creadas posteriormente no tengan más permisos de lo normal.

citations.quote: Undo the above, so that subsequently-created tables won't have any more permissions than normal
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA myschema REVOKE SELECT ON TABLES FROM PUBLIC;

sentences.text: Conviene tener en cuenta que los privilegios por defecto por esquema solo pueden añadir privilegios a la configuración global, no eliminarlos.

citations.quote: per-schema default privileges can only add privileges to the global setting, not remove privileges granted by it.

questions.question: What is a prepared statement and how do I create one in SQL?

sentences.text: PREPARE creates a prepared statement.

citations.quote: PREPARE creates a prepared statement.

sentences.text: A prepared statement is a server-side object that can be used to optimize performance.

citations.quote: A prepared statement is a server-side object that can be used to optimize performance.

sentences.text: When the PREPARE statement is executed, the specified statement is parsed, analyzed, and rewritten, and when an EXECUTE command is subsequently issued, the prepared statement is planned and executed.

citations.quote: When the PREPARE statement is executed, the specified statement is parsed, analyzed, and rewritten.
When an EXECUTE command is subsequently issued, the prepared statement is planned and executed.

sentences.text: Prepared statements can take parameters: values that are substituted into the statement when it is executed, and when creating the prepared statement, refer to parameters by position, using $1 , $2 , etc.

citations.quote: Prepared statements can take parameters: values that are substituted into the statement when it is executed.

sentences.text: For example, an INSERT prepared statement can be created and executed as `PREPARE fooplan (int, text, bool, numeric) AS INSERT INTO foo VALUES($1, $2, $3, $4);` followed by `EXECUTE fooplan(1, 'Hunter Valley', 't', 200.00);`.

questions.question: ¿Cómo agrego una columna con valor por defecto a una tabla existente?

sentences.text: Para agregar una columna con un valor por defecto no nulo, se puede usar ALTER TABLE con ADD COLUMN y DEFAULT, como en el ejemplo de la documentación.

citations.quote: To add a column with a non-null default:

sentences.text: El ejemplo es ALTER TABLE measurements ADD COLUMN mtime timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now();

citations.quote: ADD COLUMN mtime timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now();

sentences.text: Las filas existentes se llenan con la hora actual como valor de la nueva columna, y luego las filas nuevas reciben la hora de su inserción.

citations.quote: Existing rows will be filled with the current time as the value of the new column, and then new rows will receive the time of their insertion.

sentences.text: En general, la nueva columna se llena inicialmente con el valor por defecto que se indique, o con null si no se especifica DEFAULT.
